source_note: Chinese hot-topic candidates are collected from public trend pages; English wording is matched to supplied official English headlines when possible, otherwise suggested neutrally.

topics.official_english: Set-top boxes may soon become obsolete as TVs add built-in cable functions
topics.why_hot: A high-ranking livelihood and technology topic: the headline suggests Chinese households may no longer need a separate cable/set-top box, with a related Baidu entry ('电视机将内置机顶盒功能') pointing to televisions integrating that function. Two entries on the same board on the same day indicate strong public interest in simpler, cheaper home TV service.
topics.share_angle: Explain how set-top boxes work today, why integrating the function into TVs could change living-room hardware and subscription habits, and what questions consumers should ask about compatibility, cost and who controls the interface. Frame as a consumer-tech shift, not a confirmed nationwide rollout.

topics.chinese_topic: 日本高市内阁全体阁僚提交辞呈
topics.official_english: Japan PM Takaichi reshuffles cabinet; all ministers submit resignations
topics.why_hot: Two of the day's top Baidu entries cover the same story from different angles — a cabinet reshuffle by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi and the collective resignation of all cabinet ministers that precedes a reshuffle. Japanese domestic politics is a recurring high-interest international topic for Chinese audiences.
topics.share_angle: Offer a plain-language primer on how Japanese cabinet reshuffles work procedurally (collective resignation, reappointment), what the headline does and does not tell us about policy direction, and what to watch next. Avoid speculating about named ministers or policy outcomes not stated in the headline.

topics.official_english: Fed rate move draws attention to gold prices
topics.why_hot: A short but high-signal finance headline linking a U.S. Federal Reserve rate decision with gold — a pairing that reliably drives Chinese retail interest in savings, jewelry and gold investment.
topics.share_angle: Use it as an explainer hook: why gold often reacts to U.S. interest-rate expectations, how a stronger dollar and higher rates can pressure gold, and why gold still draws Chinese household demand. Be explicit that the headline alone does not specify the size, direction or timing of the Fed action.

topics.chinese_topic: 湖南航空 充电宝起火
topics.official_english: Power bank fire reported on a Hunan Airlines flight
topics.why_hot: Aviation safety plus a device almost every traveler carries: a reported power-bank fire on a Hunan Airlines flight combines a concrete safety incident with practical concern for air passengers.
topics.share_angle: Focus on the safety rules rather than the incident details: why lithium batteries and power banks are restricted in cabins, what IATA and airline rules typically require, and what passengers should do if a device overheats. Flag that details of this specific event are not established by the headline alone.

topics.official_english: Zhang Yiming reportedly becomes Asia's richest person
topics.why_hot: Wealth rankings tied to China's tech sector consistently trend; the headline places ByteDance's founder at the top of Asia's rich list, which ties into broader questions about platform economics and founder wealth.
topics.share_angle: Use it to explain how such rankings are compiled and why valuations of privately held companies are estimates, not audited numbers. Discuss the tech-industry context rather than the individual's personal life. Note the source uncertainty around any specific fortune figure.

topics.chinese_topic: 国乒被困日本机场 孙颖莎直接开练
topics.official_english: Chinese table tennis team stranded at Japanese airport; Sun Yingsha trains on the spot
topics.why_hot: Sports plus travel disruption plus a well-known athlete: two Baidu entries describe Chinese national teams (table tennis and badminton) stuck at a Japanese airport, with players improvising training and self-organizing. It overlaps with Asian Games travel coverage.
topics.share_angle: Frame as a behind-the-scenes look at elite athlete logistics and contingency planning on the road: how teams keep up training when schedules break, and what travel delays mean for competition preparation. Keep to what the headlines state; avoid speculating about blame or event scheduling.

topics.chinese_topic: 胖东来员工中秋福利：每人7箱
topics.official_english: Pang Dong Lai staff receive seven boxes each as Mid-Autumn Festival benefit
topics.why_hot: Pang Dong Lai, a Henan retailer known for generous staff treatment, reliably generates discussion about labor welfare and corporate culture in China. The headline is concrete and festival-tied, making it easy for audiences to grasp.
topics.share_angle: Use it to talk about Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival workplace customs and why this particular retailer keeps going viral for employee benefits. Compare typical holiday-benefit practices without presenting this case as representative of all Chinese employers.

topics.chinese_topic: 多年了 我们为什么执着于挖运河
topics.why_hot: An infrastructure-and-economy explainer style headline that has drawn wide attention: canal projects are a visible, long-running element of Chinese water transport and regional development planning.
topics.share_angle: Turn it into a geography-and-economics explainer: what inland waterway shipping offers compared with road and rail, why canal projects take decades, and the trade-offs around water use and ecology. Keep it explanatory rather than advocacy, and avoid citing project costs or completion dates not given in the source headline.
